blogs.title: Ciminelli's Shadow: Defining Protected Property Interests in Securities Fraud
blogs.description: This post analyzes the Fifth Circuit's reliance on the Supreme Court's 2023 decision in Ciminelli to distinguish between the impermissible 'right-to-control' theory and the permissible 'fraudulent-inducement' theory. It examines why the deprivation of economic information alone is insufficient to sustain a fraud charge, but why inducing followers to purchase securities satisfies the requirement of depriving a victim of a traditional property interest.

blogs.title: Intent to Profit, Not Harm: Kousisis Reshapes the Mens Rea of Federal Fraud
blogs.description: Focusing on the 'intent to defraud' element, this post discusses the court's application of the Supreme Court's 2025 decision in Kousisis. It explores how the ruling rejects the requirement that a fraudster must intend to cause net economic loss to the victim, establishing that a defendant's intent to obtain money or property through deception is sufficient even if the victim receives something of value in return.

blogs.title: The Digital Pump and Dump: Prosecuting Social Media Schemes Under 18 U.S.C. § 1348
blogs.description: This post considers the broader implications for securities enforcement in the age of 'finfluencers.' It evaluates how the Fifth Circuit's reversal signals that traditional mail and wire fraud concepts borrowed by the securities fraud statute (18 U.S.C. § 1348) are adaptable to modern social media manipulation tactics, providing a roadmap for future indictments against digital trading schemes.
